problem:
The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=3,$ and ${x}_{4}=-4$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$ Determine the **expanded form** of $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,108$
worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=3,$ and ${x}_{4}=-4,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-3)(x-3)(x-3)(x-(-4)) \\  & =(x-3)(x-3)(x-3)(x+4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)(x-3)(x-3)(x+4) & =({x}^{2}-6x+9)({x}^{2}+x-12) \\  & ={x}^{4}+{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-6{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+72x+9{x}^{2}+9x-108 \\  & ={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+81x-108.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+81x-108.$
